original_question: Fix an integer n > 2. Define Phi_G on subsets S of the vertex set V of an undirected graph G = (V, E) by Phi_G(S) = S union {v in V | there exist distinct s0, s1 in S with {s0, v} and {s1, v} both edges of G}. A graph is propagative if for every two-element subset S of V there exists k >= 1 such that Phi_G^k(S) = V. Determine the smallest integer m such that every undirected graph with n vertices and minimum degree at least m is necessarily propagative.
target_in_paper: Puzzle 3.1.2 in §3.1 ('Preparation: Propagative graphs'), together with the preceding Definition 3.1.1. Its sharp resolution is supplied immediately afterward by Example 3.1.3 and Proposition 3.1.4.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right graph-theoretic target very closely: it matches the paper's closure operation on subsets of vertices, the definition of a propagative graph via 2-element seeds and iteration of that operation, and the fixed-n minimum-degree threshold problem that the paper isolates as a stand-alone puzzle.
missing_details: The paper poses this as Puzzle 3.1.2 in §3.1, i.e. as a purely graph-theoretic subproblem used later in the proof of the main Aufhebung theorem, not as the main theorem itself.

For full stand-alone fidelity, say explicitly that G is a finite simple undirected graph on exactly n vertices; the paper's graph convention is simple graphs (edges are 2-element subsets of the vertex set).
It is slightly cleaner to declare Phi_G as a self-map Phi_G: P(V) -> P(V), and to say that Phi_G^k denotes k-fold iteration.

The paper's sharp threshold is phrased via the cutoff 'minimum degree > n/2' (shown sharp by Example 3.1.3 and Proposition 3.1.4); if one insists on an integer threshold, that becomes m = floor(n/2) + 1.
If you want maximal paper-faithfulness, include the exact quantifier structure: for every 2-element subset S of V, there exists k >= 1 such that Phi_G^k(S) = V.
refined_question: Fix an integer n > 2. Let G = (V,E) be a finite simple undirected graph with |V| = n, and define a map Phi_G: P(V) -> P(V) by Phi_G(S) = S union {v in V : there exist distinct s0, s1 in S with {s0,v} in E and {s1,v} in E}. Call G propagative if for every subset S subseteq V with |S| = 2, there exists k >= 1 such that Phi_G^k(S) = V. Determine the sharp minimum-degree threshold for propagativity: what is the smallest integer m = m(n) such that every n-vertex graph G with minimum degree delta(G) >= m is necessarily propagative?
justification: This is the exact graph-theoretic subproblem isolated in the paper. Section 3.1 first introduces the closure operator and the notion of a propagative graph (Definition 3.1.1), then asks precisely for the minimum-degree threshold at fixed n (Puzzle 3.1.2). The surrounding context confirms that this is not a side variant invented by your draft but a deliberate ingredient of the paper's main proof: §1.3 highlights Proposition 3.1.4 as the graph-theoretic phenomenon used to obtain the sharp upper bound for the Aufhebung, and §3.4 later invokes it again through Proposition 3.4.4. Example 3.1.3 gives the lower-bound obstruction via bipartite graphs, while Proposition 3.1.4 gives the matching upper bound, so your draft is aimed at exactly that local question.
